display.description:
Share of completed requests that did not return HTTP 5xx over the last five minutes. This is request-based availability, not measured uptime.

Measurement details:
1 minus the fraction of completed HTTP requests with 5xx responses. Excludes health/metrics routes. This is not uptime; timeouts before instrumentation and no traffic are not measured. Missing input stays empty.
display.name: Requests without server errors

spec.query: 100 * (1 - ((sum by (cluster_name,service_name) (rate(http_server_requests_total{cluster_name=~"${app_cluster}",service_name=~"${instrumented_service}",http_route!~"(?i).*(health|ready|live|metrics).*",http_response_status_code=~"5.."}[5m])) or on (cluster_name,service_name) (0 * sum by (cluster_name,service_name) (rate(http_server_requests_total{cluster_name=~"${app_cluster}",service_name=~"${instrumented_service}",http_route!~"(?i).*(health|ready|live|metrics).*"}[5m])))) / (sum by (cluster_name,service_name) (rate(http_server_requests_total{cluster_name=~"${app_cluster}",service_name=~"${instrumented_service}",http_route!~"(?i).*(health|ready|live|metrics).*"}[5m])) > 0)))

display.description:
1 means errors consume the allowed budget at the planned rate; 10 means ten times that rate. Compare both windows and your agreed availability target.

Measurement details:
Error fraction divided by the configured error budget. 1x consumes budget at the allowed rate; 14.4x sustained in both windows is a common fast-burn investigation signal. The default target is 99.9%; set slo.availabilityTarget to your agreed objective. This chart alone does not prove a 30-day SLO or trigger paging.
display.name: How quickly errors use the allowed budget (times the allowed rate)

display.description:
Percentage of completed requests with an HTTP 5xx response. Timeouts before instrumentation may not be counted.

Measurement details:
Uses the time period selected in the top toolbar. Sums non-overlapping counter changes at the chart resolution (minimum one minute) across the selected period. This is a metric estimate, not a per-request audit. Scrape gaps, new series and unavailable history can undercount activity. Totals are rounded for display. Scrape timing and partial interval boundaries affect the result. A longer selected period includes more history; it does not change the alert evaluation windows.

Use logs or traces for the exact event and cause.

display.name: What this dashboard tells you

spec.text: **How many requests reach the application, how often do they fail, and how long do they take?** Choose an application, then compare traffic, errors and response time. These measurements come from instrumentation inside the application. Health-check routes are excluded. No traffic cannot prove availability. **No data is not the same as zero.** Select a cluster before narrowing the next filters. **None** selects nothing; **Everything** selects all available values. After changing a cluster, reset the following filters to Everything. Full names and values opens the complete resource list.

display.description:
Compare typical and slow-request response times. A rising tail can reveal slow requests hidden by the average.

Measurement details:
p50 covers half the calls, p95 covers 95%, and p99 covers 99%. Without completed calls, no response time can be calculated.
display.name: Response time over time (ms)

display.description:
Traffic grouped by response type. HTTP 4xx usually indicates a rejected client request; HTTP 5xx indicates a server-side failure.

Measurement details:
2xx means success; 3xx means redirection; 4xx needs client or authentication context; 5xx means a server error.
